dashboard.summary: Open the qym platform dashboard from the CLI.
dashboard.when_to_use: Use this when a local or CI workflow should hand off into the platform UI for run review, comparison, or debugging.
failure_modes: Use `--no-open` in remote shells or CI runners where launching a browser is not possible.
If `QYM_PLATFORM_URL` is unset, the command falls back to the local platform default.
next_steps: Use `qym run list --json` when you want scriptable run discovery instead of opening the UI.

submit.summary: Upload a saved results file to the platform.
submit.when_to_use: Use this when a run finished offline or on another machine and you need to ingest the artifact into the shared platform.
failure_modes: A valid `QYM_API_KEY` or `--api-key` is required for protected platform deployments.
The file must match a qym-supported CSV or JSON results format.
next_steps: Open the dashboard or the run detail page after upload to verify item counts and metrics.

run.summary: Create, inspect, and compare evaluation runs.
run.when_to_use: This is the primary CLI noun for day-to-day evaluation work.

run create.summary: Execute a new evaluation run from a Python task function and a dataset.
run create.when_to_use: Use this for local experiments, CI checks, larger benchmark jobs, and multi-model comparisons.
examples: qym run create --task-file examples/example.py --task-function my_task --dataset my-set --metrics exact_match,fuzzy_match
qym run create --task-file examples/csv_dataset_eval.py --task-function my_task --dataset-csv ./qa.csv --metrics exact_match

common_flags.purpose: Use a named remote dataset such as a Langfuse dataset.
common_flags.when: Choose this when the dataset already lives in your shared evaluation backend.

common_flags.purpose: Use a local CSV file as the dataset source.
common_flags.when: Choose this for offline work, rapid local iteration, or air-gapped evaluation.

common_flags.purpose: Select built-in or custom metrics for the run.
common_flags.when: Always set this deliberately instead of relying on ad hoc defaults.

common_flags.purpose: Emit structured output instead of only human-readable console text.
common_flags.when: Use this in automation, CI, or other agentic workflows.

failure_modes: Exactly one of `--dataset` or `--dataset-csv` should be provided for a normal run.
Judge metrics require `QYM_JUDGE_MODEL` and a compatible API key configuration.
Task import failures usually mean the module path or function name is wrong.
exit_codes: Execution failed after argument parsing succeeded.
Usage error such as missing required flags or conflicting arguments.
next_steps: Use `qym run get <run_id> --json` or the platform UI to inspect item-level results.
Use `qym analyze run <run_id>` once you have failures worth clustering.

run tasks.summary: List distinct task names discovered in the platform.
run tasks.when_to_use: Use this before filtering large run sets or when a teammate already streams runs into the platform.

run list.summary: List recent evaluation runs from the platform.
run list.when_to_use: Use this as the entry point for browsing, filtering, or selecting run IDs in scripts.
failure_modes: This command depends on platform connectivity and a valid API key when auth is enabled.

run get.summary: Fetch detailed data for a single run.
run get.when_to_use: Use this when another workflow already knows the run ID and you need the resolved payload.

run failed.summary: Return only failed or errored items from a run.
run failed.when_to_use: Use this for first-pass triage before you open the full run or trigger AI analysis.

run compare.when_to_use: Use this when you want to understand regressions between prompts, models, or datasets.

metric.when_to_use: Use this before creating a new evaluation plan or onboarding a new task.

metric list.when_to_use: Use this for authoritative metric discovery in scripts or docs.

analyze.summary: Run AI-assisted analysis over completed runs.
analyze.when_to_use: Use this after a run completes and you need structured clustering or summaries instead of raw failures.

analyze run.summary: Trigger item-level root-cause analysis for a run.
analyze run.when_to_use: Use this when you want categorized explanations and suggested fixes for failing items.
failure_modes: The user profile or platform deployment needs a valid LLM analysis configuration.
Large runs may take longer if the platform queues analysis work.

analyze summary.summary: Get an aggregated AI summary for a run.
analyze summary.when_to_use: Use this for a concise narrative you can share in release notes or model review conversations.

config.summary: Inspect or validate local platform configuration.
config.when_to_use: Use this before depending on platform operations from a new machine, CI runner, or offline environment.

config show.summary: Show the resolved configuration used by the SDK and CLI.
config show.when_to_use: Use this to see what environment resolution actually produced after `.env` and shell overrides.

config check.when_to_use: Use this before running production or CI evaluations so failures happen early.
failure_modes: Failures usually mean the platform URL, API key, auth mode, or TLS reachability is wrong.
next_steps: Check the environment matrix in Deploy & Operate if connectivity or auth still fails.
